title: 1956 AHSME Problem 4
statement: A man has \(\$10{,}000\) to invest. He invests \(\$4{,}000\) at \(5\%\) and \(\$3{,}500\) at \(4\%.\) In order to have a yearly income of \(\$500,\) he must invest the remainder at:

solutions.text:
The amount left to invest is \[ 10000-4000-3500=2500. \] The first two investments earn \(0.05(4000)+0.04(3500)=340\) dollars, so the remaining investment must earn \(500-340=160\) dollars. Its required rate is \[ \frac{160}{2500}=0.064=6.4\%. \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: First find both the uninvested principal and the income still needed
The first two investments earn \(\$200\) and \(\$140\) per year
